kept.excerpt: Banco de México’s Governing Board decided unanimously to maintain the target for the overnight interbank interest rate at 6.50%. Headline inflation was still expected to converge to the target in the second quarter of 2027. The balance of risks for the trajectory of inflation within the forecast horizon remained biased to the upside.
kept.relevance: The latest policy decision before the cutoff establishes the 6.50% reference level and the Board’s unanimous stance entering the period before the August meeting.

kept.excerpt: Mexico’s annual inflation rate decelerated for an eighth consecutive fortnight in early July. Twelve-month inflation reached 3.10%, compared with the 3.12% forecast in a Reuters poll. Annual core inflation was 3.95%, returning within the central bank’s 3%, plus or minus one percentage point, target range.
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day report provides the most recent eligible inflation evidence bearing on the case for maintaining the policy rate.

kept.excerpt: Mexico’s annual inflation rate fell in June for the third consecutive month, reaching its lowest level since December 2020. Annual prices slowed more than expected and settled into the central bank’s target range, easing pressures to hike rates. Banxico had held its benchmark interest rate at 6.5% in a unanimous decision late in June.
kept.relevance: The June inflation release documents the disinflation trend available to policymakers before the August decision.

kept.excerpt: BBVA expected Banxico to keep the policy rate unchanged at 6.50% and reiterate that the current stance would remain in place for an extended period while monitoring services inflation. It judged that significant economic slack was unlikely to receive much weight now that the policy rate had reached neutral. Soft labor market conditions were expected to support core services disinflation.
kept.relevance: This dated expert preview explains the economic rationale for a prolonged pause and identifies persistent services inflation as a key consideration.

kept.excerpt: All 30 economists in a Reuters poll conducted between June 18 and June 22 expected Banxico to maintain its benchmark interest rate at 6.50% at its June 25 meeting. The report noted that Banxico had lowered its 2026 economic growth forecast to 1.1% from 1.6%.
kept.relevance: The poll measures the breadth of the hold consensus preceding the latest completed policy meeting, while the growth forecast provides context for reluctance to tighten.

kept.excerpt: Banxico cut the policy rate by 25 basis points to 6.50% and confirmed the end of the easing cycle, although the decision revealed a divided Board. The easing bias in forward guidance was dropped. The statement said that it would be appropriate to maintain the reference rate at its current level.
kept.relevance: This account of the preceding rate cut establishes the transition from easing to a stated preference for holding rates.

kept.excerpt: Mexico’s annual inflation rate reached 3.55% in the first half of June, below the 3.77% expected in a Reuters poll. Capital Economics analyst Kimberley Sperrfechter said the larger-than-expected decline would ease pressure on Banxico to raise interest rates in the near term. She nevertheless expected a modest tightening cycle to begin near the end of the year.
kept.relevance: This report provides a contrasting expert outlook in which future tightening remained possible but was expected later than the August meeting.

search_notes: Evidence frozen at 2026-07-23, inclusive. Publication dates were verified from indexed source headers, dated documents, or Reuters datelines; BBVA’s June preview webpage is dated June 25, while its linked PDF is dated June 24. Only pre-cutoff material is included, with no prediction-market pages, odds, market prices, or subsequent meeting developments. Broad search results surfaced later material, which was excluded. Full-page web_fetch failed because of a provider configuration error, and the requested agent-reach fallback returned RATE_LIMITED; excerpts therefore rely on source text exposed by web_search and are concise factual paraphrases. A final supplementary search failed with HTTP 500. The live official calendar and minutes indexes were not included because they contain later entries and do not provide a verified pre-cutoff publication date for the schedule itself. No independently verified August-specific economist poll published by the cutoff was found; the included poll concerns the June meeting.
